review_evidence: Original Zidd-authored English content; NCERT structural alignment reviewed against the source map
title: Gone with the Scooter
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. All teaching passages, prompts, examples, answers, and rubrics are original Zidd-authored content and do not copy the textbook body.

levels.title: Follow a chain of events
levels.focus: track event order and identify the main idea
levels.teaching_goal: Use time clues and linked actions to explain what happened first, next, and finally.

guided_check.teaching_block: Sequence words such as first, next, and finally show the order of events. Find the action that follows the first event.
guided_check.passage: First, Mira tied labels to the sports bags. Next, she placed them beside the court. Finally, the coach checked each label.
guided_check.prompt: What did Mira do after tying the labels?
options: She placed the bags beside the court.
accepted_answers: She placed the bags beside the court.
placed the bags beside the court
put the bags beside the court

bridge.teaching_block: When time words are absent, follow cause and result. The object changes hands in a logical order.
bridge.passage: A whistle rolled under a bench. Dev spotted it and gave it to the announcer. The announcer returned it to the games teacher.
bridge.prompt: Name the first event and the final event in the whistle's journey.

concept_slots.description: States that the whistle rolled under a bench.
any_of: the whistle rolled under the bench
a whistle went under the bench

concept_slots.description: States that the announcer returned the whistle to the games teacher.
any_of: announcer returned it to the games teacher
announcer gave the whistle to the games teacher
it was returned to the games teacher
the games teacher got the whistle back

masterclass.teaching_block: A main idea joins the most important events instead of listing every small detail. Link the ball's movement to the unexpected result.
masterclass.passage: At a community court, a foam ball bounced through an open gate. It dropped into the rear crate of a delivery scooter. The rider left before the players noticed where the ball had gone.
masterclass.prompt: State the main idea and give two events that build it.

concept_slots.description: Explains that linked events caused the ball to leave with the scooter.
any_of: ball accidentally left with the scooter
ball was carried away by a scooter
a chain of events took the ball away
foam ball went away in the scooter crate

concept_slots.description: Names the ball bouncing through the open gate.
any_of: foam ball crossed the open gate
it bounced out through the gate

concept_slots.description: Names the ball landing in the scooter crate before the rider left.
any_of: rider left with the ball in the crate

independent_check.teaching_block: Read this new scene without choices. Reconstruct the order from the actions and their results.
independent_check.passage: A library return card slipped from Anaya's notebook. A gust pushed it across the footpath, and it caught in the basket of a parked bicycle. The librarian found it there after lunch.
independent_check.prompt: Retell the card's journey in the correct three-step order.

concept_slots.description: Begins with the card slipping from the notebook.
any_of: return card fell from the notebook
it slipped out of Anaya's notebook
the card came out of the notebook

concept_slots.description: Continues with the gust pushing the card across the footpath.
any_of: gust pushed it across the footpath
wind blew the card across the path
a gust carried it across the footpath

concept_slots.description: Ends with the card in the bicycle basket and the librarian finding it.
any_of: librarian found it in the basket
it was found in a parked bicycle's basket

forbidden_phrases: Anaya put it in the basket

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply sequence thinking to an unfamiliar setting. Keep only the cause, movement, and outcome.
transfer_check.passage: During a picnic, Rafi set his cap on a low wall. A sudden breeze lifted it onto the roof rack of a waiting bus. The bus moved to the next parking lane before anyone saw the cap.
transfer_check.prompt: Summarize how the cap changed place from beginning to end.

concept_slots.description: Identifies the cap's starting place on the wall.
any_of: cap was on a low wall
Rafi set his cap on the wall
it rested on a low wall

concept_slots.description: Identifies the breeze carrying the cap to the bus.
any_of: breeze lifted it onto the bus
wind blew the cap to the roof rack
it landed on the bus roof rack

concept_slots.description: Identifies the bus moving away with the cap.
any_of: cap went to the next lane on the bus
it left on the bus roof rack

levels.title: Infer a fair choice
levels.focus: use evidence to explain motives and responsible actions
levels.teaching_goal: Infer why a character acts responsibly and support the reason with a detail from the scene.

guided_check.teaching_block: An inference combines a character's action with a sensible reason. A name label is evidence about ownership.
guided_check.passage: Ishaan found a badminton racket beside the stairs. He read the name label and carried the racket to the school office.
guided_check.prompt: Why was taking the racket to the office a responsible choice?
options: The office could return it to the named owner.
The racket was too heavy to carry home.
The stairs were closed for cleaning.
accepted_answers: The office could return it to the named owner.
the office could return it
so it could reach its owner

bridge.teaching_block: A fair check uses a detail that the true owner is likely to know. Explain both the action and its purpose.
bridge.passage: Two pupils said a lunch box was theirs. Farah asked each pupil to describe the sticker hidden underneath before she handed it over.
bridge.prompt: Why did Farah ask about the hidden sticker?

concept_slots.description: Explains that the hidden sticker could identify the real owner.
any_of: find out whose lunch box it was
the owner would know the sticker
only the real owner might describe it

concept_slots.description: Explains that Farah wanted to avoid giving the box to the wrong person.
any_of: avoid giving it to the wrong pupil
hand it to the correct person
not choose between them by guessing

masterclass.teaching_block: Strong reasoning separates evidence from assumption. Name what the character did and what that action protected.
masterclass.passage: Kavya noticed a scooter key near the market gate. She gave it to the security guard and described the exact spot, but she did not post a photograph of the key online.
masterclass.prompt: What can you infer about Kavya's purpose? Support your answer with two details.

concept_slots.description: Infers that Kavya wanted the key returned safely to its owner.
any_of: wanted to return the key safely
wanted the owner to get the key back
tried to protect the lost key

concept_slots.description: Uses giving the key to security as evidence.
any_of: gave it to the security guard
security guard could keep it safe

concept_slots.description: Uses withholding the photograph as evidence that claimants must prove ownership.
any_of: owner would need to describe the key
a false claimant could not copy the photo

independent_check.teaching_block: Infer the motive in a fresh situation. Pair the responsible action with direct evidence from the passage.
independent_check.passage: On a crowded bus, Naman saw a woollen scarf on an empty seat. He told the conductor the seat number and left the scarf with her instead of carrying it away.
independent_check.prompt: Why did Naman leave the scarf with the conductor, and which detail supports your reason?

concept_slots.description: Explains that the conductor could help return the scarf to the passenger.
any_of: help the owner get it back
keep it safe for the passenger
lost property should stay on the bus

concept_slots.description: Uses Naman reporting the seat number or leaving the scarf as evidence.
any_of: told the conductor the seat number

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer fair-reason thinking beyond lost objects. Explain why checking evidence is better than guessing.
transfer_check.passage: After a gardening activity, three seedling trays had missing labels. Sana compared leaf shapes with the class observation chart before replacing the labels.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain why Sana checked the chart before labelling the trays.

concept_slots.description: Explains that the chart provided evidence for identifying each seedling.
any_of: she could compare the leaves with the chart

concept_slots.description: Explains that checking prevented incorrect or guessed labels.
any_of: make sure each label was correct

levels.title: Unlock action words
levels.focus: infer word meanings from context and use precise vocabulary
levels.teaching_goal: Use nearby action and result clues to infer meanings and apply precise words in new sentences.

guided_check.teaching_block: A context clue can be a sound, action, or result near an unfamiliar word. Loose objects that knock again and again rattle.
guided_check.passage: As the scooter crossed the rough lane, an empty bottle rattled inside its metal crate.
guided_check.prompt: What does rattled mean in this sentence?
accepted_answers: made repeated knocking sounds
made a repeated knocking sound
made quick clattering sounds

bridge.teaching_block: Look at the movement around the word. A rider who turns quickly to avoid something swerves.
bridge.passage: Leela swerved around a deep puddle, then guided her bicycle back into a straight line.
bridge.prompt: Which meaning of swerved fits the passage?
options: rode faster in a straight line
accepted_answers: turned suddenly to one side
turned quickly to one side
changed direction suddenly

masterclass.teaching_block: Prove a meaning with the result in the sentence. If an object cannot slide or fall, it has been secured.
masterclass.passage: Meera secured the parcel with two straps. Even on the bumpy road, it stayed firmly in the carrier.
masterclass.prompt: Explain what secured means and name the clue that proves it.

concept_slots.description: Explains that secured means fastened or made safe from moving.
Uses the parcel staying firm on the bumpy road as evidence.
any_of: did not move on the bumpy road

independent_check.teaching_block: Infer a new word without choices. Use both the action and what happened immediately after it.
independent_check.passage: The kitten darted beneath the chair when the tray clanged. In less than a second, only its tail was visible.
independent_check.prompt: What does darted mean here, and which detail supports your meaning?

concept_slots.description: Explains that darted means moved very quickly or suddenly.
Uses the less-than-a-second detail as evidence.
any_of: the passage says less than a second

transfer_check.teaching_block: Carry the meaning into your own sentence. First infer fastened, then use the related word secure accurately.
transfer_check.passage: Before the van left, Omar fastened the folding ramp with a strong latch and tugged it twice to check it.
transfer_check.prompt: Explain fastened in this context, then write a new sentence using secure with the same general meaning.

concept_slots.description: Explains that fastened means fixed or closed firmly.
Uses secure in a new sentence about making an object safe or firm.

levels.title: Connect reasons and contrasts
levels.focus: use because and but to build complete linked sentences
levels.teaching_goal: Choose and use connectors that show reason or contrast while keeping every sentence complete.

guided_check.teaching_block: Because introduces a reason. The words after because should explain why the first action happened.
guided_check.passage: Aarav slowed the scooter ___ a puppy was crossing the lane.
guided_check.prompt: Which connector completes the sentence with a reason?
accepted_answers: because

bridge.teaching_block: But joins contrasting ideas. The second idea is different from what the first idea leads us to expect.
bridge.passage: The basket looked full, ___ there was still room for the small parcel.
accepted_answers: but

masterclass.teaching_block: A strong linked sentence can contain both a reason and a contrast. Check that each connector expresses the intended relationship.
masterclass.passage: Ria wanted to cycle home. Rain had started. She wore a raincoat. She still waited until the road was safe.
masterclass.prompt: Combine the ideas into one complete sentence using because for the reason and but for the contrast.

concept_slots.description: Uses because to connect the rain with wearing a raincoat.
any_of: wore a raincoat because rain had started
wore her raincoat because it was raining
because the rain had started she wore a raincoat
because it started raining Ria wore a raincoat

concept_slots.description: Uses but to contrast wanting to cycle with waiting for safety.
any_of: but she waited until the road was safe
wanted to cycle but waited for a safe road
but Ria still waited for safety
but did not leave until the road was safe

forbidden_phrases: because the road was safe she waited

independent_check.teaching_block: Build a complete reason sentence from a new context. Include who acted, what they did, and why.
independent_check.passage: Clouds covered the sky before the science club's rooftop observation. The teacher moved the telescope into the covered corridor.
independent_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence using because to explain the teacher's action.

concept_slots.description: States that the teacher moved the telescope to the covered corridor.
any_of: teacher moved the telescope into the covered corridor
teacher took the telescope to the covered corridor
telescope was moved into the covered corridor

concept_slots.description: Uses because to connect the action to the cloudy sky.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use both relationships in an unfamiliar sports scene: because for the cause and but for the unexpected response.
transfer_check.passage: The relay began late because the track was wet. The team did not stop preparing; they continued their warm-up under the shelter.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence about the delay and the team's response using both because and but.

concept_slots.description: Uses because to explain that the wet track delayed the relay.
any_of: relay began late because the track was wet
relay was delayed because of the wet track
because the track was wet the relay began late
because rain left the track wet the relay was delayed

concept_slots.description: Uses but to show that the team kept warming up despite the delay.
any_of: but the team continued warming up
but they kept preparing under the shelter
but the runners did not stop their warm-up

levels.title: Build precise event sentences
levels.focus: control word roles, past tense, and sentence order
levels.teaching_goal: Arrange nouns, verbs, adjectives, and time clues into clear sentences about completed events.

guided_check.teaching_block: An adjective describes a noun. In the phrase silver scooter, silver tells us more about the scooter.
guided_check.passage: A silver scooter waited beside the narrow gate.
accepted_answers: silver

bridge.teaching_block: A past-tense verb shows an action that is complete. Look for the word that tells what the subject already did.
bridge.passage: Rohan checked the loose mirror before yesterday's ride.
bridge.prompt: Which word is the past-tense action verb?
accepted_answers: checked

masterclass.teaching_block: A clear order is subject, action, then useful detail. Place the adverb close to the action it describes.
masterclass.passage: carefully / the courier / closed / the metal box
masterclass.prompt: Put the words in order to make one complete sentence.
accepted_answers: The courier carefully closed the metal box.
The courier carefully closed the metal box
The courier closed the metal box carefully.
The courier closed the metal box carefully

independent_check.teaching_block: Arrange this fresh set of words without choices. Keep the completed action in the past tense.
independent_check.passage: after the bell / the pupils / quietly / entered / the hall
independent_check.prompt: Arrange the words into a complete sentence with correct order and punctuation.
accepted_answers: The pupils quietly entered the hall after the bell.
The pupils quietly entered the hall after the bell
After the bell, the pupils quietly entered the hall.
After the bell the pupils quietly entered the hall

transfer_check.teaching_block: Turn notes into a new past-tense sentence. Include a noun, an adjective, an action, and a time clue.
transfer_check.passage: Notes: careful cyclist / yellow raincoat / wave to the guard / yesterday
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete past-tense sentence using all four notes.

concept_slots.description: Uses cyclist as the sentence subject and includes careful.
Includes the adjective-noun phrase yellow raincoat.
Uses waved as the completed action toward the guard.
Includes yesterday as the time clue.

levels.title: Summarize without copying
levels.focus: select the main event, cause, and outcome for a concise summary
levels.teaching_goal: Write a brief original summary that keeps the central problem, response, and result.

guided_check.teaching_block: A good summary keeps the central event and outcome. It leaves out minor colours, times, and repeated details.
guided_check.passage: A fruit seller's scooter would not start near the school gate. Two older pupils helped push it to a safe corner, where a mechanic tightened a loose cable.
guided_check.prompt: Which option is the best summary?
options: Pupils helped move a stalled scooter safely, and a mechanic fixed its loose cable.
A scooter stood near a school gate beside a fruit seller.
Two older pupils walked past a corner where a mechanic worked.
A fruit seller carried fruit while pupils discussed a cable.
accepted_answers: Pupils helped move a stalled scooter safely, and a mechanic fixed its loose cable.
pupils helped move a stalled scooter and a mechanic fixed the cable

bridge.teaching_block: Build a summary around the problem and the response. Combine related details instead of copying each sentence.
bridge.passage: A stack of art boards blocked the activity-room doorway. The class moved the boards onto a shelf, then marked a clear path with tape.
bridge.prompt: Write one sentence that summarizes the problem and the class's response.

concept_slots.description: States that art boards blocked the doorway or path.
any_of: boards were blocking the activity room
stack of boards blocked the path
doorway was blocked by art boards

concept_slots.description: States that the class cleared and marked the path.
any_of: class moved them to a shelf
marked a clear path with tape
moved the boards and marked the path

forbidden_phrases: the boards stayed in the path

masterclass.teaching_block: A complete summary answers three questions: What changed? Why did it matter? What was the result? Use your own sentence structure.
masterclass.passage: A delivery rider noticed that a paper bag was tearing at the bottom. She stopped before the crossing, placed the bag inside a reusable box, and delivered every item without damage.
masterclass.prompt: Summarize the problem, the rider's response, and the result in 18 to 30 words.

concept_slots.description: Identifies that the paper bag was tearing.
any_of: bottom of the bag was breaking

concept_slots.description: States that the rider transferred the bag or items to a reusable box.
any_of: placed it inside a reusable box
moved the items to a box
protected the bag with a reusable box
used a box to hold the delivery

concept_slots.description: States that all items arrived without damage.

independent_check.teaching_block: Summarize this new problem-solving scene independently. Keep the difficulty, the pupils' response, and the outcome.
independent_check.passage: The robotics club's cart stopped halfway to the library because one wheel was trapped by too many heavy books. The pupils divided the books between two smaller carts, freed the wheel, and reached the library on time.
independent_check.prompt: Write an 18 to 30 word summary in your own words.

concept_slots.description: Identifies that an overloaded cart or trapped wheel stopped the trip.
any_of: wheel was trapped by heavy books
cart could not move because of the books

concept_slots.description: States that the pupils divided the books between smaller carts.
any_of: divided the books between two carts
shared the load between two carts

concept_slots.description: States that the wheel was freed and the pupils arrived on time.
any_of: freed the wheel and arrived on time

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer summary writing to a science-and-garden context. Compress the warning, repair, and result into one clear account.
transfer_check.passage: A moisture monitor warned Class 5 that the garden pipe was leaking beside the seedlings. The class closed the tap, replaced the cracked connector, and restarted watering after checking the soil. The seedlings remained healthy.
transfer_check.prompt: Write a 20 to 35 word summary that includes the problem, response, and outcome.

concept_slots.description: Identifies the warning about a leaking pipe near the seedlings.
any_of: monitor warned about a leaking pipe
garden pipe leaked beside the seedlings
class found a cracked pipe connector

concept_slots.description: States that the class stopped the water and replaced the connector.
any_of: closed the tap and replaced the connector
stopped the leak and repaired the pipe
fixed the connector before watering again

concept_slots.description: States that watering resumed safely and the seedlings stayed healthy.

items.passage: At the repair booth, Zoya filled the tyres first, tightened the bell next, and tested the brakes last.
items.prompt: What did Zoya do immediately before testing the brakes?
accepted_answers: She tightened the bell.
tightened the bell

items.passage: A red token fell beside the ticket table. Nia picked it up and handed it to the volunteer wearing the token pouch.
items.prompt: Where did the token fall, and who received it?

concept_slots.description: Identifies that the token fell beside the ticket table.
Identifies the volunteer with the token pouch as the receiver.
any_of: Nia gave it to the volunteer

items.passage: The neighbourhood club painted bright lane markers, added two mirrors at the sharp turn, and placed a guard near the exit. Cyclists could now move through the lane more safely.
items.prompt: Which sentence states the paragraph's main idea?
options: The club made a cycling lane safer in several ways.
The mirrors were brighter than the lane markers.
A guard painted two mirrors near an exit.
Cyclists preferred the sharp turn to the straight lane.
accepted_answers: The club made a cycling lane safer in several ways.
the club made the lane safer

items.passage: Pooja noticed that the notice-board corners were curling in the wind. She pinned each corner, covered the board with a clear sheet, and checked it after the rain. Every notice stayed readable.
items.prompt: State the main idea and one detail that supports it.

concept_slots.description: States that Pooja protected the notices from wind and rain.
any_of: she kept the notice board safe from weather
Pooja made sure the notices stayed readable
she stopped the notices from being damaged

concept_slots.description: Names pinning corners, adding a clear sheet, or checking after rain.
any_of: covered the board with a clear sheet

items.passage: When Adil saw a helmet hanging from the park fence, he asked the guard to record it in the lost-property book.
items.prompt: What is the most reasonable inference about Adil?
options: He wanted the owner to be able to find the helmet.
He planned to borrow the helmet without asking.
He believed the fence needed a decoration.
He was trying to close the park early.
accepted_answers: He wanted the owner to be able to find the helmet.
he wanted to help the owner
he wanted the helmet returned

items.passage: The class found an unsigned poster entry. Instead of guessing the artist, Vani compared the drawing code with the submission list.
items.prompt: What can you infer about Vani's decision, and what evidence supports it?

concept_slots.description: Infers that Vani wanted an accurate or fair identification.
any_of: wanted to identify the artist accurately
tried to find the correct artist

concept_slots.description: Uses comparing the code with the submission list as evidence.
any_of: matched the code with the list

items.passage: A parcel label was smudged, but the flat number remained clear. The courier called the building desk before choosing a door.
items.prompt: Which answer gives the best reason for the courier's call?
options: The courier called because the desk could confirm the correct door from the flat number.
The courier called because the parcel was too light to carry.
The courier called because every door was already open.
The courier called because the label needed a brighter colour.
accepted_answers: The courier called because the desk could confirm the correct door from the flat number.
the desk could confirm the correct door

items.passage: During a class exhibition, a model bridge began to lean. Rehan held the base while Dia added two supports, and the visitors were asked to wait until the model was stable.
items.prompt: In 35 to 55 words, explain why the pupils paused the visitors and how their actions solved the problem. Use evidence from the passage.
items.preflight_rule: The response must be an original 35 to 55 word explanation that links the leaning model to visitor safety and explains how holding the base and adding supports made it stable.

rubric_criteria.description: Explains that visitors were paused because the leaning model was unstable or unsafe.
Uses Rehan holding the base as relevant evidence.
Uses Dia adding two supports as relevant evidence.
Explains that the combined actions made the model stable before viewing resumed.
Uses clear complete sentences and a logical reason link.

items.passage: The old gate creaked as the caretaker pushed it, producing a long rough sound.
items.prompt: What does creaked mean in this passage?
accepted_answers: made a long rough sound
made a rough squeaking sound
made a creaking sound

items.passage: Tara glimpsed the bus number just before it turned the corner, so she saw it only for a moment.
items.prompt: What does glimpsed mean here?
accepted_answers: saw briefly
saw for a moment
looked at quickly
caught a quick sight of it
noticed briefly

items.passage: The mechanic inspected the cable closely before saying that it was safe to use.
items.prompt: Which sentence uses inspected with the same meaning?
options: The nurse inspected the bandage for loose edges.
The singer inspected loudly during the song.
The puppy inspected across the garden at noon.
The rain inspected the empty road.
accepted_answers: The nurse inspected the bandage for loose edges.
the nurse inspected the bandage

items.passage: The equipment cupboard must be made safe before the room is locked.
items.prompt: Write a sentence using secure to show that someone fastens or protects an object.

concept_slots.description: Uses secure or secured as a verb.
Names a reasonable object that is fastened or protected.

items.passage: The driver moved slowly ___ the road was narrow.
items.prompt: Which connector gives the reason for moving slowly?
accepted_answers: because

items.passage: The team wanted to practise outside. A strong wind began. They moved into the hall.
items.prompt: Write one complete sentence using because to explain the move and but to show the contrast.

concept_slots.description: Uses but to contrast the wish to practise outside with moving indoors.
any_of: wanted to practise outside but moved into the hall
team wanted to be outside but went into the hall
but they moved into the hall
but the team practised in the hall

concept_slots.description: Uses because to connect the move with the strong wind.

items.passage: Which option is a complete sentence about a finished delivery?
items.prompt: Choose the complete sentence.
options: The rider delivered the medicine before noon.
accepted_answers: The rider delivered the medicine before noon.
the rider delivered the medicine before noon

items.passage: Notes: Nisha / return the library key / to the librarian / after class
items.prompt: Turn all the notes into one complete sentence.

concept_slots.description: Uses Nisha as the subject.
States that Nisha returned the library key to the librarian.
any_of: returned the library key to the librarian
gave the library key back to the librarian
returned the key to the librarian

concept_slots.description: Includes after class as the time detail.

items.passage: The careful guard lifted the heavy barrier.
items.prompt: Which set correctly labels careful, guard, and lifted?
accepted_answers: adjective, noun, verb
adjective noun verb

items.passage: Use these words: bright / lamp / flashed
items.prompt: Write a complete sentence, then identify the adjective, noun, and verb.

concept_slots.description: Uses all three words in a complete sentence.
Uses and identifies bright as the adjective.
Uses and identifies lamp as the noun.
Uses and identifies flashed as the verb.

items.passage: Yesterday, the volunteers ___ every bicycle tag before the event began.
items.prompt: Which verb correctly completes the past-time sentence?
accepted_answers: checked

items.passage: Notes: last evening / Priya / notice a loose strap / tighten it
items.prompt: Write one complete past-tense sentence using the notes.

concept_slots.description: Uses noticed as a past-tense action by Priya.
any_of: Priya saw that the strap was loose

concept_slots.description: Uses tightened as the completed response.
Includes the past-time clue last evening.

items.passage: quietly / the mechanic / tested / the repaired horn
items.prompt: Which option puts the words in a clear sentence order?
options: The mechanic quietly tested the repaired horn.
Quietly the repaired tested mechanic horn.
The repaired horn the mechanic quietly.
Tested quietly horn the mechanic repaired.
accepted_answers: The mechanic quietly tested the repaired horn.
the mechanic quietly tested the repaired horn

items.passage: before sunset / returned / the borrowed pump / Harsh / to the sports room
items.prompt: Arrange the words into one complete sentence.
accepted_answers: Harsh returned the borrowed pump to the sports room before sunset.
Harsh returned the borrowed pump to the sports room before sunset
Before sunset, Harsh returned the borrowed pump to the sports room.
Before sunset Harsh returned the borrowed pump to the sports room

items.passage: A sudden shower soaked the cardboard signs for the school walk. The volunteers moved the signs indoors, dried them under fans, and covered each one with a reusable plastic sleeve before the walk began.
items.prompt: Which sentence best summarizes how the volunteers saved the signs?
options: Volunteers rescued rain-soaked signs by drying and covering them before the school walk.
A school walk began after a sudden shower near some cardboard.
Fans and plastic sleeves were stored indoors by volunteers.
The volunteers made new signs because the old words were incorrect.
accepted_answers: Volunteers rescued rain-soaked signs by drying and covering them before the school walk.
volunteers dried and covered the wet signs before the walk

items.passage: The eco-club's collection cart became stuck in soft mud while carrying paper to the recycling room. Four pupils removed half the bundles, laid two flat boards under the wheels, and pushed the lighter cart onto the paved path. They then carried the remaining bundles separately.
items.prompt: Write a 45 to 70 word summary in your own words. Include the problem, the main solution steps, and the final outcome without copying full sentences.
items.preflight_rule: The response must be an original 45 to 70 word summary that identifies the cart stuck in mud, explains lightening it and using boards, and states that the cart reached the paved path while the remaining bundles were carried separately.

rubric_criteria.description: Identifies that the paper cart became stuck in soft mud.
Explains that pupils removed bundles to make the cart lighter.
Explains that boards were placed under the wheels to help move the cart.
States that the cart reached the paved path and the remaining paper was carried separately.
Uses connected original sentences and keeps only important events.
